subject: Senior data pros are learning AI faster than juniors
body:
Our platform data revealed: Who’s learning what, and the one place juniors are ahead.

The Output by DataCamp ( https://www.datacamp.com?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=261020_1-senior-vs-junior-data-prof--na--engagement_2-mix_6-tier-2_8-emal-ci_11-weekly-news&dc_euid=20788339 )

A weekly dispatch for AI + Data Practitioners · #018

*****************************************************************************************
42% of senior data professionals started an AI course this year. Only 25% of juniors did.
*****************************************************************************************

 

Four in ten senior data professionals started an AI course this year, against one in four early-career learners. In AI and machine learning roles, juniors are moving faster: their adoption grew by 19.3 percentage points in a year, against 14.3 among seniors.

Both groups are learning AI. They're learning different parts of it.

We examined what each group studied over two 12-month windows. Early-career learners lean toward the building blocks: the OpenAI API, prompt engineering, Hugging Face, LLMOps. Seniors prioritise the finished tools: Microsoft Copilot, scalable agentic systems, LangChain, and responsible AI. You'd assume the newest agentic tooling would be picked up by people newest to the field. It isn't. Claude Code 101 is studied more by experienced professionals than by people early in their careers.

Production work still falls to the people who've been doing it longest.

 

42% of senior data professionals started an AI course this year. Only 25% of juniors did. ( https://www.datacamp.com/tracks/ai-fundamentals?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=261020_1-senior-vs-junior-data-prof--na--engagement_2-mix_6-tier-2_8-emal-ci_11-weekly-news&dc_euid=20788339 )

 

That pattern doesn't hold in every role. Juniors are gaining ground in data science and AI/ML, where AI is already the work. In analytics, BI, and data engineering, where most early-career data people actually sit, seniors are pulling further ahead. Data engineering shows the widest gap: seniors are now 2x more likely than juniors to be learning AI for it.

Separately, PwC finds the most AI-exposed entry-level roles are now 7x more likely to ask for skills like leadership and strategic thinking. This is the applied, judgment-heavy end of the work, and the end juniors are studying least.

Put the two together, and the pattern is clear: employers are asking more of entry-level roles, and junior upskilling isn't keeping pace just yet.

subject: Your interview answer is polished. So is everyone else’s.
body:
Our co-founders on what interviewers are actually looking for now.

The Output by DataCamp ( https://www.datacamp.com?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=261013_1-radar-best-moments--na--engagement_2-mix_6-tier-2_8-emal-ci_11-weekly-news&dc_euid=20788339 )

A weekly dispatch for AI + Data Practitioners · #017

Calendar

Flash Sale | 50% Off on Yearly Plan! Save Now ( https://www.datacamp.com/promo/limited-time-sale-october-26?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=261013_1-radar-best-moments--na--engagement_2-mix_6-tier-2_8-emal-ci_11-weekly-news&dc_euid=20788339 )

Co-founder Ask Me Anything

*****************************************
Standing out when everyone comes prepared
*****************************************

 

Interviewers now assume you prepared with AI.

That's the view of DataCamp co-founder and CEO Jonathan Cornelissen. A polished answer no longer sets you apart, because the next candidate prepared the same way. What sets you apart now is the depth of insight you bring.

Jonathan said this at the close of RADAR 11x, where he and fellow co-founder and COO Martijn Theuwissen answered live questions on jobs, hiring, and what a career looks like now that AI tools are everywhere.

 

Co-founder AMA: Standing out when everyone comes prepared ( https://www.datacamp.com/podcast/the-best-moments-from-radar-11x?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=261013_1-radar-best-moments--na--engagement_2-mix_6-tier-2_8-emal-ci_11-weekly-news&dc_euid=20788339 )

 

Martijn couldn't think of anyone he knows with strong AI skills who lost their job, even during cuts. If you can automate part of your role, you can take on more, and that makes you harder to replace.

Take data analysts, a role plenty of people are writing off. Martijn sees a different direction: "judgment in the role will be more important." Companies still need analysts, but the job is shifting from dashboards and code to framing the question, directing the tool, and checking what comes back.

For analysts, he predicts two paths. The first is data engineering, because as more people run their own analysis, someone has to build the infrastructure behind it. The second is AI engineering, building the agents and tools everyone else uses. AI engineer roles are up 255% year over year in our State of AI Careers research.

Regardless of role, judging the quality of output is now a valuable skill.

Jonathan's reasoning: the software analysts used to write behaved the same way every time, so you could reason about whether it worked. Modern AI systems don't. Martijn's more direct: understand the concepts underneath, or "you're just going to accept what the model produces."

It's tempting to ship what the model gives you. Spotting what's missing before anyone else does is quickly becoming the skill leaders value most.

We've condensed their session, and highlights from the rest of the day, into a single podcast. Worth an hour while you plot your next move. […]

subject: Lens Extensions are back, and AI builds them
body:
Hi Hamza,
Extensions are back in Lens K8S IDE, and this time your AI tool writes them for you.
Build one by describing it. Choose Create new and name your extension. Lens sets up the project and opens it in your AI tool, whether that is Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, or OpenCode.
Install one from the Marketplace. Browse the Marketplace in the navigator, install with a click, or clone one that almost does what you want and change it with your AI tool.
Our picks to start with, built by the Lens team
Production Cluster Mark
A red edge around the window when you are on production.
Lens Glance
Describe a dashboard, and your AI tool builds it live in Lens.
GitHub Actions
CI runs behind each cluster, and an alert when a deploy fails.
Colima
Deploy, start, and stop local Kubernetes from the navigator.
Lens Glance and Colima run on macOS and Linux. GitHub Actions needs the GitHub CLI.
If you are on Lens Enterprise
Extensions stay off until an administrator turns them on, so if you do not see them yet, ask your Lens administrator. Anyone can publish an extension, so install only from publishers you trust.
👉 See Extensions governance
Also new
Google Kubernetes Engine. Your GKE clusters, right in Lens. Sign in with your Google account, pick a project, and Lens finds every cluster in it, ready to open with a click. No gcloud to install, no kubeconfig to copy, no keys to manage.
👉 Learn about adding GKE clusters
Extensions and the GKE integration are premium features, included with Lens Plus, Pro, and Enterprise, and available on a Personal plan with an active 14-day trial.

subject: Thank you for applying to Redwood Materials
body:
Hi hamza,

Thank you for your interest in Redwood Materials! Your email has been received and we're excited that you would consider joining our team.

Redwood’s goal is to develop and deploy new technologies for dramatically increasing the scope and scale of recycled and sustainable materials in global supply chains. We’re passionate about building a sustainable future and changing the world with a small team. With that said, we’re thrilled that you’re excited about helping us solve this super important and difficult environmental problem.

We will review your information as soon as we can and we'll be in touch if your qualifications align with our needs. Due to the volume of emails received, we want to be respectful of your time and let you know that we will only be reaching out to candidates whose skillsets best match our roles. If our team feels that you’re a fit, we will contact you shortly about next steps. If you don’t hear back immediately, don't worry! We're growing fast and will have new roles opening up in the future, so please keep an eye on our website for updates!

Recycle with Us

Redwood’s focus is to take both end-of-life electric vehicle batteries and other lithium-ion powered consumer devices and then recycle, refine, and remanufacture them into new products here in America. The largest lithium and cobalt mines in the western hemisphere can be found in the junk drawers of America and we’re on a mission to collect as many of these old products as possible. We encourage all candidates, visitors, and guests to bring old phones, laptops, tablets, electric toothbrushes, and any other rechargeable device with a lithium-ion battery. For more information about our consumer recycling program, please visit our website ( https://www.redwoodmaterials.com/recyclewithus ). 

Thanks,
Redwood Recruiting

*******************************************************************
Data scientist down 50%. AI engineering up 4x. Coding didn't budge.
*******************************************************************

 

Since late 2023, we've asked every DataCamp learner the same question: What role are you aiming for? Over 90,000 have answered.

 

Data scientist down 50%. AI engineering up 4x. Coding didn't budge. ( https://www.datacamp.com/tools/ai-careers-gap?utm_source=customerio&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=261006_1-skills-shift--na--engagement_2-mix_6-tier-2_8-emal-ci_11-weekly-news&dc_euid=20788339 )

 

Learners are moving away from data science and toward AI engineering. Since 2024, the share aiming to be a data scientist has halved, while AI engineering has quadrupled.

What hasn't changed is the code. People chasing AI jobs are the most code-heavy of the four groups: 71% of the courses they start involve code, against 68% for aspiring data scientists, 61% for data engineers, and 51% for data analysts. Job titles are moving fast. The skills behind them aren't.

Fewer people aiming for data science doesn't mean the analysis work has disappeared. Agentic AI has put data-driven decision-making within reach of people who aren't data scientists, so the work has been spread out, not cut. It still happens, it's just no longer one team's job. And coding skills are holding steady for a simple reason: to build with AI tools, you need to understand what they produce. You can't fix code you can't read.

Universities are seeing the same shift. New computer-science majors in the US fell 13% in a year. In the UK, computing acceptances dropped 9%, the first fall in seven years, while AI course acceptances rose 39%. Similarly, IT intake in the Netherlands has declined by more than 20% since 2022, and Australia saw 21% fewer students choosing ICT degrees in 2026. Enrollment is still rising, so this isn't students leaving university. They're moving toward AI, not away from technical work.

subject: Deine Bewerbung auf die Stelle Cloud Platform Entwickler (m/w/d)
body:
Hallo hamza,
nochmals vielen Dank für deine Bewerbung und dein Interesse, deine Power bei ALDI Nord einzubringen.
Nach eingehender Prüfung deiner Unterlagen müssen wir dir leider mitteilen, dass wir zurzeit keine Möglichkeit sehen, dich deinen Wünschen und Qualifikationen entsprechend in der ausgeschriebenen Stelle einzusetzen.
Wir bedauern, dir keine positive Nachricht geben zu können und bedanken uns für deine Zeit und Mühe, die du in deine Bewerbung investiert hast.
Du bist weiterhin überzeugt davon, dass deine POWER zu uns passt? Dann bewirb dich gerne erneut auf andere Stellen auf unserer Karriere-Website. Wir sind stets auf der Suche nach zukünftigen ALDIanern und freuen uns, dich vielleicht in einem anderen Team begrüßen zu dürfen.
Alles Gute!
Dein Karriere-Team
